(1) Fresh-device flow: cleared localStorage + valid magic token at /analysis/AAPL?autorun=1&t=<token> -> EXACTLY 1 POST /api/auth/magic returning 200, sai_token populated (188 chars), sai_user populated, NO redirect to /login, AAPL BUY verdict renders ($271.06, $305 target, $255 stop loss), 0 console errors. (3) Already-logged-in user redeeming a fresh token: 1 POST returning 200, JWT refreshed (different token from the seeded one), session preserved as admin (jolor69@gmail.com), AAPL verdict renders, 0 console errors. The StrictMode double-fire bug from iter 25 is FULLY RESOLVED — all 3 runs show exactly ONE POST /api/auth/magic per flow. SEPARATE MINOR ISSUE FOUND (non-blocking, called out per request): in flows 1 and 3 the final URL ends up as /analysis/AAPL?t=<token> — i.e. autorun=1 is dropped (consistent with iter 25 observation) AND the t= param is somehow re-added back (NEW). The AuthContext code clearly calls params.delete('t') + window.history.replaceState, but a downstream React Router navigation (likely Analysis page consuming autorun=1 via navigate(pathname, {replace:true}) using router-stored location state which still includes t=) appears to overwrite the cleaned URL. Token is already-consumed/useless so it's not exploitable, but it does leak a one-time token into history/share/bookmarks.

integration_issues.flow: URL cleanup after magic redemption (downstream Analysis page navigation)
integration_issues.issue: After successful magic redemption, AuthContext calls history.replaceState to strip ?t=<token> while preserving autorun=1. Observed final URL is /analysis/AAPL?t=<token> — autorun=1 is dropped AND t= is restored. Likely cause: Analysis page consumes autorun=1 via React Router navigate(pathname, {replace: true}); React Router's stored location.search still contains the original '?autorun=1&t=<token>' (because history.replaceState bypasses React Router's history listener) and the navigate call reapplies it without autorun=1. Result: a one-time-use, already-consumed magic token is left in the URL (no security impact since token is consumed, but it leaks into browser history, shares, and bookmarks). Severity: LOW. Not blocking the auth fix per user instructions.

action_items: (LOW / OPTIONAL) Fix URL cleanup race so the final URL is /analysis/AAPL?autorun=1 (no t=, with autorun preserved). Two clean fixes: (a) After AuthContext calls history.replaceState, also call window.dispatchEvent(new PopStateEvent('popstate')) so React Router picks up the new search; or (b) Move the redemption + URL cleanup INTO a route-aware effect using react-router's useNavigate({replace:true}) so router state stays in sync; or (c) In Analysis page, when consuming autorun, read params from window.location.search (post-cleanup) rather than from router state. Confirmed not blocking this iteration's auth fix.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext.jsx StrictMode fix: clean useRef-based single-fire guard at line 18-22. The guard sets bootstrappedRef.current=true synchronously BEFORE any await, so the second StrictMode invocation short-circuits immediately. Verified live — exactly 1 POST /api/auth/magic across all 3 test flows.

AuthContext.jsx setBootstrapping(false) is now reached on every code path (success branch line 53, catch fallthrough via line 75/87). Intent is clearer; no more reliance on the catch-branch fallthrough.
Minor: AuthContext.jsx line 64-69 catch branch's URL strip duplicates the success-branch logic. Could be DRYed into a small helper stripMagicTokenFromUrl(), but not critical.

rca of the issue: Iter 25 root cause (StrictMode double-fire causing duplicate POST /auth/magic + 401 race) is RESOLVED by the useRef guard at AuthContext.jsx line 18-22. The guard sets bootstrappedRef.current=true synchronously before the async work begins, so React.StrictMode's intentional second mount-effect invocation short-circuits on line 21 and never re-reads window.location nor re-POSTs the magic token. Verified live with network capture: exactly 1x POST /api/auth/magic per flow across 3 separate test runs (fresh-device, bogus-token, logged-in-user).
